title: LCA Definition
question: What is the Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) of two nodes in a binary tree?
searchIntent: what is lowest common ancestor binary tree
realWorldScenario: LCA is used in phylogenetic trees, version control merge-base detection, and hierarchical organization lookups.

title: LCA of Binary Tree
question: How do you find the LCA of two nodes in a general binary tree (not BST)?
realWorldScenario: If left and right recursion both return non-null, current node is the LCA. O(n) recursive approach.

title: LCA of BST
question: How do you find the LCA of two nodes in a BST? How is it simpler than for a general binary tree?
realWorldScenario: For BST: if both nodes < root → go left; if both > root → go right; else → current root is LCA. O(log n).

title: LCA with Parent Pointers
question: How would you find the LCA if each node has a parent pointer?
searchIntent: find LCA with parent pointer java
realWorldScenario: Build ancestor path to root using a HashSet; traverse from the other node upward until first common ancestor is found.

title: LCA for n-ary Tree
question: How would you extend the LCA algorithm to an n-ary tree (each node has multiple children)?
searchIntent: lowest common ancestor multiple children java
realWorldScenario: Iterate over all children; if more than one child returns a target found signal, current node is LCA.
